entry.summary: Visa-free short stays: Liechtenstein is one of the four non-EU Schengen members, reached through Switzerland or Austria.
entry.max_stay: 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen area
entry.other: Schengen Entry/Exit System: fingerprints and photo at the border on first entry (free, nothing to do beforehand). Get an entry stamp where one is still given, and carry your passport across internal borders.

visa-preparation.entry_summary: Visa-free (entry via Switzerland - Schengen rules apply).
visa-preparation.fastest_entry: No visa: Liechtenstein is reached through Switzerland or Austria (it's a Schengen member), so the Schengen 90 days in 180 rule applies in practice.
steps: There's no airport; arrive through Zurich or another Schengen airport.
At the first Schengen border, give fingerprints and a photo for the Entry/Exit System (EES); it's free.
Stays over 90 days need a national visa or a bilateral waiver arranged before travel.

items.text: Using a narcotic, or possessing it for your own use, is an offence tried by the Landgericht: a fine of up to CHF 50,000, or up to 6 months' prison if unpaid (BMG art 21). In minor cases the court may waive the penalty.
Cannabis with 1% THC or more counts as a narcotic. Unlike Switzerland, there is no fixed-fine procedure or 10 g rule.

laws.rule: Using a narcotic, or possessing it for your own use, is an offence tried by the Landgericht: a fine of up to CHF 50,000, or up to 6 months' prison if unpaid (BMG art 21). In minor cases the court may waive the penalty. Cannabis with 1% THC or more counts as a narcotic. Unlike Switzerland, there is no fixed-fine procedure or 10 g rule.
